incident-bot: [ALERT] realtime latency regression detected for /v1/generate (eu-west). p95=720ms, p99=1.82s, threshold breaches on p99 for last 5m. AlertID=rbw-ALRT-8921

sara (oncall): paging the team, joining bridge now :phone: https://zoom/incident-1753210000

mike (sre): on it — pulling live dashboards and traces. Which models/routes impacted?

sara (oncall): looks concentrated on streaming routes and a handful of long-tail requests hitting seq_len>1024. KV cache hit rate dropped from ~92% to 48% around 1753209800.

jon (eng-runtime): seeing increased worker queue depth and slow io on a subset of pods. stacktraces show stalls in the attention kernel fallback path. forwarding recent flamegraph link: https://grafana/sg/flame/1753210000

mike (sre): quick mitigation options: 1) shift some traffic off the EU cluster to EU-fallback nodes, 2) reduce max_batch_size for streaming routes, 3) temporarily disable prefix caching writes to avoid cache thrash. Thoughts?

sara (oncall): start with route shift 20% to eu-fallback and reduce batch size to 8 for streaming. set up monitoring for error rate and tail latency.

jon (eng-runtime): doing route shift now: ```
# shift 20% traffic to fallback pool
redwoodctl traffic shift --from=eu-prod --to=eu-fallback --percent=20 --routes="/v1/stream" --reason="p99 spike"
```

alicia (cs): FYI I already got two N1 tickets from enterprise customers in EU complaining about slow responses (one report at 1753209955). I'll message affected accounts and set expectations.

mike (sre): applying batch size override: ```
redwoodctl config set --scope=route:/v1/stream --key=max_batch_size --value=8 --ttl=10m
```

jon (eng-runtime): also toggled prefix-cache writes off on the EU pool to see if hit-rate stabilizes: ```
redwoodctl feature toggle --pool=eu-prod --feature=prefix_cache_writes --state=off
```

sara (oncall): monitoring dashboards — p99 dropped to 1.1s after shift and batch change, still above SLO but trending. error rate unchanged.

mike (sre): digging into KV cache telemetry — the spike correlates with a large rollout earlier today that increased model variants and caused cache fragmentation. will revert that small rollout if rollback path available.

nina (pm): which rollout? I pushed a small model-variant test at 1700 today for A/B. If that's the cause we should rollback the variant for EU. Impact on metrics?

jon (eng-runtime): identified rollout id=mv-2024-11-07-21. Reverting variant for EU only: ```
redwoodctl rollout revert --id=mv-2024-11-07-21 --region=eu-west --confirm
```

alicia (cs): customers notified. One customer asked for ETA; saying we're doing traffic shift and rollback, monitoring.

sara (oncall): handing incident to mike for live mitigations/cleanup. I'll remain on call for handover. Next steps: 1) observe 15m post-rollback, 2) if stable, ramp traffic back by 10% every 5m, 3) create follow-up postmortem with KV cache metrics and rollout analysis.

mike (sre): ack. creating a short incident artefact and paging eng-runtime for follow-up deep-dive tomorrow. Collecting traces and sample requests for retest. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident note appended: "traffic-shifted, batch_size reduced, prefix_cache_writes disabled, rollback initiated for mv-2024-11-07-21 (eu-west)." Ticket created: INC-1753210000

jon (eng-runtime): saving heap/profile dumps and trace samples to /artifacts/inc-1753210000 for postmortem.

sara (oncall): last update before handover: p99=980ms, p95=420ms, error rate steady. handing to mike.

mike (sre): taking over. will keep channel updated and escalate if regressions return.

nina (pm): thanks team — please add impact notes and customer list to the postmortem.

alicia (cs): logged impacted customers: AcmeCorp, BrightApp, NovaPay. Outreach in progress.

mike (sre): final note: root suspected = cache fragmentation caused by model-variant rollout; immediate fix = rollback + traffic shift. Postmortem owner: jon (eng-runtime)."
